PyFixest 0.70 moves the state of a fitted model out of loose private attributes
such as `fit._se`, `fit._vcov`, or `fit._N` into typed components: `fit.model`,
`fit.options`, `fit.sample_info`, `fit.coeftable`, `fit.variance_covariance`,
`fit.fitstat`, `fit.sandwich`, `fit.first_stage`, and others. Each component is
documented in the [API reference](/reference/index.qmd).

The compatibility layer preserves the names listed below while you migrate:

- Most listed names are **deprecated aliases**. They reconstruct the former
  representation from the current fit and emit a `PyfixestDeprecationWarning`
  that names the replacement. They do not rerun the 0.60 estimator.
- Some 0.60 representations are no longer supported. Their names are **removed**:
  reading them raises an `AttributeError` that explains why and names the
  replacement.

```{python}
import warnings

import pyfixest as pf
from pyfixest.errors import PyfixestDeprecationWarning

data = pf.get_data()
fit = pf.feols("Y ~ X1 + X2 | f1", data, vcov={"CRV1": "f1"})

with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
    warnings.simplefilter("always")
    old = fit._se

print(caught[0].message)
print((old == fit.coeftable.se).all())
```

## How to find deprecated attributes in your code

`PyfixestDeprecationWarning` is a `FutureWarning`, so Python shows it by
default. To find reads of aliases whose warnings are enabled, turn the
warning into an error, for example in your test suite:

```{python}
#| eval: false
warnings.simplefilter("error", PyfixestDeprecationWarning)
```

With pytest, add `"error::pyfixest.errors.PyfixestDeprecationWarning"` to the
`filterwarnings` setting instead.

## Attributes no longer supported

`FixestFormula`, `_k_fe`, `_fe`, `na_index`, `_Yd`, `_Xd`, `_Zd`,
`_endogvard`, `_fixef_dict`, and `_alpha` raise `AttributeError`. The table
below lists their replacements. In particular, use `fit.fixef()` for labelled
fixed-effect coefficients and `fit.fixef_counts.n_levels_by_fe` for counts.
The former IV `first_stage()` method is now the `fit.first_stage` component.

## Attributes whose values can change

- `_fml`, `_model_name`, `_fixef`, and `_model_spec` reflect the current
  formula and fixed-effect encoding. `_na_index` raises after separation;
  use `fit.sample_info.dropped_row_index` for all dropped rows.
- `_support_crv3_inference` and other capability aliases reflect current
  support. For DID2S, `_vcov_type`, `_clustervar`, `_is_clustered`, and `_G`
  reflect current clustering. Numerical aliases such as `_rmse` and `_se`
  reflect estimation and inference changes in the [changelog](/changelog.qmd).

## Names still read by other packages

Aliases used by released versions of [marginaleffects](https://github.com/vincentarelbundock/pymarginaleffects)
and [maketables](https://github.com/py-econometrics/maketables) are marked
silent in the table and do not warn yet. No removal version is scheduled.

## All deprecated names

The table shows which model classes each name applies to. Entries for `Feols`
also apply to IV, GLM, and quantile models, unless a more specific entry is listed.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from pyfixest.estimation.models._deprecated_attributes import (
    DEPRECATED_ATTRIBUTES,
    Removed,
)

print("| Old attribute | Model classes | Use instead | Status |")
print("|---|---|---|---|")
for attribute in DEPRECATED_ATTRIBUTES:
    for class_name, entry in attribute.classes.items():
        if isinstance(entry, Removed):
            status = f"Removed: {entry.reason}"
        else:
            status = "Deprecated alias" + (" (silent)" if attribute.silent else "")
        print(
            f"| `fit.{attribute.name}` | `{class_name}` "
            f"| `{entry.replacement}` | {status} |"
        )
```
